questions.prompt: Amine and I share one desk. Complete: "We tidy ___ desk at the end of every lesson."
questions.explanation: The owners are Amine and the person speaking, that is we, and the possessive adjective of we is our: we tidy our desk. The forms "we" and "us" are the people who do or receive the action and never stand in front of a noun, and "their" would give the desk to other people, when the text says the two of them share it.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: "Tomorrow we ___ the classroom."
questions.explanation: The future is will plus the bare verb, so the promise is "we will tidy". After will the verb never takes the -s of the present ("will tidies"), never the -ing form ("will tidying") and never the word to ("will to tidy").

questions.prompt: Amine is 10, Sarra is 11 and Karim is 12. Which sentence about Amine is correct?

options.text: Amine is younger of the three.
Amine is the younger of the three.
Amine is the youngest of the three.
Amine is youngest than the others.

questions.explanation: Amine is 10, so he is under both Sarra at 11 and Karim at 12: he beats the whole group, and that is the superlative the + young + est. The forms "younger" and "the younger" compare only two people, and "youngest than" glues the superlative to the word than, which belongs to the comparative alone.

questions.prompt: Which of these job names is built from a verb plus the ending -er?
questions.explanation: The verb build gives the person who does it: build + er = a builder. The word "a carpenter" ends in the same three letters but there is no verb carpent behind it, "a doctor" ends in -or and comes from no verb either, and "a vet" is a whole word you learn as it is.

questions.prompt: Your little brother wants to hit the cat. Which sentence forbids it?
questions.explanation: To forbid something you put Don't in front of the bare verb: Don't hit the cat. Starting with "Not" copies the negative word of another language, "You hit the cat" is a statement about what he does and not an order at all, and after Don't the verb stays bare, so "hitting" cannot follow it.
